production.note: US model years of the 4.3-litre car. First: Edmunds lists the 2006 V8 Vantage '2dr Coupe (4.3L 8cyl 6M)' at '380 hp @ 7,300 rpm'. Last: AstonMartins.com (astonmartins-v8-vantage-4-3, enthusiast site) lists '2006MY, 2007MY, 2008MY' and says the car 'was replaced with an improved 2009MY version' with a '4.7 litre V8 engine'; Edmunds lists the 2009 car as '4.7L' with '420 hp' (edmunds-v8-vantage-2009). Split from the 4.7-litre car (2009 on) because the engine changed (4.3 to 4.7 litres) as well as the rating; the 4.7-litre range is held back for lack of qualifying sources. UK build began autumn 2005.

body.note: Two-seat coupe. The V8 Vantage Roadster is sold under its own name and is not part of this record.

aspiration.note: Evo: 'V8 4280cc', with no turbocharger or supercharger; AstonMartins.com (astonmartins-v8-vantage-4-3): '4.3 litre quad cam 32 valve dry sumped V8 engine'.

transmission.note: Provisional (enthusiast site). AstonMartins.com: 'standard 6 speed Graziano manual gearbox'; 'Sportshift automated manual optional from 2007.5MY'. Sportshift is an automated manual. Edmunds 2006 and 2007 (edmunds-v8-vantage-2006, edmunds-v8-vantage-2007) list only the '6-speed manual' coupe. No manufacturer or magazine page confirming Sportshift for 2007-2008 US cars was opened; only one source gives it.

powerHp.note: Quote (Evo specification panel, V8 Vantage (2005)): "Power | 380bhp @ 7300rpm". Edmunds gives the US 2006 car '380 hp @ 7,300 rpm' (edmunds-v8-vantage-2006), so the US rating is the same figure. Edmunds' 2007 page prints '379 hp @ 7,000 rpm', database variations not supported by any Aston or magazine figure. The 2009-on 4.7-litre car (420 bhp) is outside this record.

weightLb.note: Step 2 of the weight order (major magazine specification panel; no Aston page with a weight could be opened). Quote (Evo specification panel, V8 Vantage (2005)): "Weight | 1630kg". 1,630 kg x 2.20462 = 3,593.5 lb, rounded to 3,594. Evo's text calls it the kerb weight: the early car's 'final kerb weight was a little disappointing at 1630kg'. AstonMartins.com (astonmartins-v8-vantage-4-3, enthusiast site) also mentions 'the 1570kg machine' and lists 'Kerb Weight: 1630 kg'. Manual coupe (standard car).

discrepancies.reason: Edmunds 2006 gives 3,461 lb (1,570 kg), a figure AstonMartins.com also mentions; Evo calls 1,630 kg (3,594 lb) the car's 'final kerb weight', and Edmunds 2007 gives 3,594 lb.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Evo's 1,630 kg, which Evo labels the kerb weight; 1,570 kg is not explained by any opened source.

provisionalNote: Transmission is provisional: the optional Sportshift (6-speed automated manual, from 2007.5MY) rests only on AstonMartins.com, an enthusiast site; Edmunds lists only the manual coupe for 2006-2007. An Aston Martin US release, brochure or magazine spec panel for a 2007-2008 V8 Vantage listing Sportshift would replace it. Power and weight rest on Evo's specification panel.
